newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom mobile sales take off in Nov.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom mobile sales take off in Nov.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG said on Friday that the introduction of new low-cost tariffs for its D1 mobile phone system had helped make November the fastest selling month in the history of its mobile communications unit.

New customers rose by a net 90,000 in November, of which 50,000 signed up for the latest "Eco" low-cost deals. A further 60,000 hired mobile phones in the first half of December, bringing total digital network users to over 2.2 million.
"The mobile phone is the front-runner in this year's Christmas shopping," Lothar Hunsel, chief executive of Deutsche Telekom MobilNet GmbH (T-Mobil), said in a statement.
T-Mobil triggered a price war among Germany's three mobile phone system operators this autumn when it launched two-year deals which almost halved rental charges.

The Telly-D1 version of the Eco tariff has a monthly rental fee of 29 marks ($18.6), down from 49 marks, and a simple billing structure for calls. There is no minimum use charge, no deactivation fee and no flat-rate for calls of less than a minute.

T-Mobil also said it still has around 600,000 subscribers to its analogue C-Tel mobile phone network, which has been declining since the launch of digital networks. It also has over one million subscribers to paging services and 100,000 users of trunked radio and satellite communications services.
In addition to building its German business, T-Mobil said it had added four foreign mobile phone licences to its stable over the past year, bringing the total to 13.
Investment abroad totals a billion marks and T-Mobil is present in North America, central and eastern Europe and Asia.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.558 German Marks)
